Autocorrelation of the Residuals

Source: R/plot_diagnostic.R
plot_acf.Rd

plot_acf() selects the graph of the sample autocorrelation of the quantile residuals, or of their squares, and plot_pacf() the graph of their partial autocorrelation, with the limits \(\pm 1.96/\sqrt{N}\). The series are the observations of each group in time order, and the autocorrelation is pooled over the groups.

Usage

plot_acf(
  lag_max = 30,
  squared = FALSE,
  by = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  legend = TRUE
)

plot_pacf(
  lag_max = 30,
  squared = FALSE,
  by = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  legend = TRUE
)

Arguments

lag_max

The largest lag.

squared

Whether to use the squared residuals.

by

NULL, or the name of the variable of the data that divides the observations into separate series.

time

NULL, or the name of the variable of the data that orders the observations within a series.

seed

A single number that seeds the randomization, or NULL.

legend

Whether to draw the legend that names the elements of the graph.

Value

A PlotAcf object, inheriting from diagnostic_plot.

Details

With residuals \(e_{gt}\) for the group \(g\) at the position \(t\) of its series, and \(\bar e\) their mean over all \(N\) observations, the autocorrelation at lag \(k\) is $$r_k = \frac{\sum_g \sum_t (e_{gt} - \bar e)(e_{g,t+k} - \bar e)} {\sum_g \sum_t (e_{gt} - \bar e)^2},$$ where the numerator sums the pairs that lie in the same group at distance \(k\) and the denominator sums every observation. Each pair counts once, so a long series weighs more than a short one, and with one group \(r_k\) is the autocorrelation of stats::acf(). The partial autocorrelations are computed from \(r_1, \dots, r_K\) by the Durbin-Levinson recursion. Under a correct model the quantile residuals are independent standard normal variables, \(r_k\) has standard deviation near \(1/\sqrt{N}\), and about five percent of the values fall outside the limits. The autocorrelation of the squares (squared = TRUE) detects a variance that depends on the past.

The groups and the order are taken from by and time when they are given; otherwise from the modelterms7::gas() or modelterms7::regime() term of the fit, if there is one; otherwise the observations form one series in the row order of the data. For a discrete family the residuals are randomized and seed makes them reproducible.

See also

plot_residuals(), diagnostics()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(t = 1:150)
dd$y <- as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.5), n = 150))
fit <- statmod(y ~ 1, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, plot_type = plot_acf(lag_max = 20))

ggplot2::autoplot(fit, plot_type = plot_pacf(lag_max = 20))


# three series of 50 observations, stored one after the other
dd$id <- rep(1:3, each = 50)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, plot_type = plot_acf(by = "id", time = "t"),
                  data = dd)
